messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan] Ensemble Samplers (#362)
parts:
I think we need to talk about granularity in these issues
and whether we need a finer-grained plan of attack as
part of the issues.

Ensemble samplers also require work on the convergence
monitoring --- wasn't that the main holdup? And also on
initialization. They'll require changing the command-line
interfaces, too.

There are two families of such algorithms:

* differential evolution and DREAM
* Goodman and Weare's walk and stretch moves

- Bob

P.S. Another, separate issue is adaptation that communicates
across chains.

On 11/4/13, 6:54 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> Admit generic ensemble sampling within Stan's sampler engine.
>
> Allows running multiple chains internally that can communicate with each other, possibly useful during adaptation.
>
> Allows ensemble samplers such as DREAM.
>
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub <https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/362>.
>

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] [stan] Ensemble Samplers (#362)
parts:
>
> I think we need to talk about granularity in these issues
> and whether we need a finer-grained plan of attack as
> part of the issues.

See the email I just sent out. Algorithms like this ideally being as generic ideas and
then are reduced to a list of dependencies and implementations which define a plan
of attack before any dev effort is made.

> Ensemble samplers also require work on the convergence
> monitoring --- wasn't that the main holdup? And also on
> initialization. They'll require changing the command-line
> interfaces, too.
>
> There are two families of such algorithms:
>
> * differential evolution and DREAM
> * Goodman and Weare's walk and stretch moves
>
> - Bob
>
> P.S. Another, separate issue is adaptation that communicates
> across chains.

The way I picture it is first extending the sampler architecture to handle an ensemble of samplers
be default (with an ensemble of one reproducing the current behavior). Then we define
ensemble I/O (initialization, output averaging, etc), argument configuration, and then
we'd be able to implement all kinds of ensemble methods quickly (not to mention communicating
adaptation).
